recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No further core FHIR source work is needed for FHIR-10711 unless CBCC later makes a new decision to restructure Consent provisions or change the purpose/securityLabel interaction.
issue_request: FHIR-10711 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core Consent. It asked whether DSTU2 Consent.except.purpose represented user access context, an obligation to attach a purpose-of-use tag, or a data tag, and suggested organizing exception elements into user-context, data-qualifier, and action groups. The final Jira resolution was "Solved by 11055."
initial_application: No source commit was found that names FHIR-10711 directly. The linked resolution issue, FHIR-11055, was explicitly applied by historical commit 0f594b3938a50781639ecd7fa5930288595d9bfe, which changed the old Consent spreadsheet source to add the approved purpose-of-use conflict sentence to the purpose and securityLabel comments. Later source refactors carried that guidance into current Consent.provision.purpose and Consent.provision.securityLabel.
additional_context: Consent is an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini, and the old DSTU2 Consent.except family is now represented by Consent.provision. FHIR-11055 already has a no-change audit commit on the combined branch; FHIR-11056 audits the same historical commit's adjacent securityLabel definition change; and later FHIR-36354 refined hierarchical security-label wording while preserving the FHIR-11055 purpose-of-use sentence. A 2019 Zulip thread discussed PurposeOfUse value-set semantics for Consent.provision.purpose but did not contradict the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source already distinguishes Consent.provision.purpose as the user's access/request context and Consent.provision.securityLabel as data labels, with the approved shared comment that data purpose-of-use tags and access-request purpose-of-use shall not conflict. Adding new grouping prose would duplicate existing guidance and is not required by the final FHIR-10711/FHIR-11055 disposition.
